statements.markdown: **Proposition 6.111 (A subpower bound for divisor counts).** *For positive integers $n,k$, $\tau(n)^k \le (k^{2^k})^k\cdot n$, or equivalently $\tau(n)\le k^{2^k}n^{1/k}$. The constant absorbs the finitely many primes below $2^k$; for larger primes, $(\nu+1)^k\le p^\nu$ controls each factor of the divisor product. This estimate is independent of the support problem. The elementary zero-run bound above already follows from a single positive support element, without this estimate or a recurrence.*
